title: Collocation and Register
tagline: Collocation, using a corpus, verb–noun and adjective–noun collocations, phrasal verbs and their formal equivalents, idioms, register, connotation and near-synonyms, translation traps and Chinglish, and academic vocabulary
summary: Knowing a word includes knowing its company: which words it goes with, in which situations it is used and what it suggests. This course covers collocation and how to check it in a corpus, idioms and fixed expressions, the vocabulary of formal and informal registers, connotation and near-synonyms, the translation traps that produce Chinglish, and the core vocabulary of academic English.

chapters.title: Collocation
chapters.summary: Why we say *heavy rain* and *make a mistake* but not *strong rain* or *do a mistake*, and how collocations differ in strength.

chapters.title: Using a corpus
chapters.summary: Concordances, frequencies and collocates from freely available corpora and dictionaries, and how to check whether a phrase is natural.

chapters.title: Verb–noun and adjective–noun collocations
chapters.summary: The high-frequency verbs *make*, *do*, *take*, *have* and *give*, and common adjective–noun pairs.

chapters.title: Phrasal verbs and their formal equivalents
chapters.summary: Phrasal verbs in everyday speech and their single-word equivalents in formal writing (*find out* and *discover*, *put off* and *postpone*).

chapters.title: Idioms and fixed expressions
chapters.summary: Idioms, proverbs, binomials (*sooner or later*) and sentence frames, how fixed they are, and when to use them.

chapters.title: Register
chapters.summary: Formal, neutral and informal vocabulary, spoken and written English, and keeping the register of a text consistent.

chapters.title: Connotation and near-synonyms
chapters.summary: *Thin*, *slim* and *skinny*, *famous* and *notorious*: how words with similar meanings differ in feeling, strength and use.

chapters.title: Translation traps and Chinglish
chapters.summary: Words and phrases translated one-to-one from Chinese that do not work in English, and how to find the natural expression.

chapters.title: Academic vocabulary
chapters.summary: The general academic words used across subjects, their collocations and word families, and how to learn them.
